items.stemHtml: A 19-year-old man has blood pressure of 164/102 mmHg. His mother developed hypertension at 20 years of age, and his maternal uncle died of a hemorrhagic stroke at 31 years of age. Serum potassium is 3.9 mEq/L. Plasma aldosterone is high and plasma renin activity suppressed. After 2 days of low-dose dexamethasone, his aldosterone falls to undetectable levels and his blood pressure falls. Genetic testing confirms the expected abnormality. Which of the following best explains why dexamethasone works?

options.label: A
options.html: Aldosterone synthase is expressed in the zona fasciculata under ACTH control

options.label: B
options.html: Dexamethasone blocks the mineralocorticoid receptor in the collecting duct

options.label: D
options.html: Dexamethasone inhibits renin release from the juxtaglomerular cells

options.label: E
options.html: The zona glomerulosa becomes newly responsive to angiotensin II

items.explanationHtml:
Early hypertension with suppressed renin and high aldosterone, a dominant family history of early hemorrhagic stroke and suppression by dexamethasone define glucocorticoid-remediable aldosteronism (familial hyperaldosteronism type I). Unequal crossing over fuses the ACTH-responsive regulatory region of 11β-hydroxylase (CYP11B1) to the coding region of aldosterone synthase (CYP11B2). Aldosterone synthase is then expressed in the zona fasciculata and driven by ACTH; suppressing ACTH with a glucocorticoid switches it off. Potassium is often normal in this disorder.

Takeaway: glucocorticoid-remediable aldosteronism: a CYP11B1/CYP11B2 chimera puts aldosterone synthesis under ACTH, so glucocorticoids suppress it.

whyNot.B: Dexamethasone has almost no mineralocorticoid-receptor activity and does not block it; that is how spironolactone works.
whyNot.C: Inhibiting 11β-HSD2 (as licorice does) would worsen mineralocorticoid excess, not reverse it.
whyNot.D: Renin is already suppressed, and dexamethasone does not act through renin.
whyNot.E: Angiotensin II responsiveness of the glomerulosa is not the driver; the abnormal enzyme is regulated by ACTH.

items.objective: Explain glucocorticoid-remediable aldosteronism through a chimeric aldosterone synthase gene under ACTH control.
